Legal end of marriage — debated in Christianity
All human life is sacred, made in God's image

walkthroughs.body_html:
Marriage is a lifelong covenant — Genesis 2:24, 'the two shall become one flesh'.

Roman Catholics see marriage as a sacrament that cannot be dissolved. The Church of England permits remarriage in some cases.

Family is the place where children are nurtured in faith. Jesus blessed children (Mark 10).

Contraception: the Roman Catholic Church teaches sex must be open to life; only natural methods are accepted (encyclical Humanae Vitae, 1968).

Most Protestant churches permit artificial contraception within marriage.

Sex outside marriage and homosexual relationships are debated: traditional teaching restricts sex to heterosexual marriage; liberal Christians embrace same-sex relationships.

Christians hold the sanctity of life: life is sacred from conception.

Abortion: most churches oppose it; Catholics teach it is always wrong; some Protestants allow it in extreme cases (rape, danger to mother).

Euthanasia: generally opposed — only God decides when life ends. Some Christians accept passive (withdrawing treatment) but not active killing. Palliative care is preferred.

mcqs.q: What is the doctrine of the Trinity?
options: The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
Christians believe in three different gods.
God is one being existing in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) — distinct in person but united in essence; Christians remain monotheistic.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.

mcqs.q: What do Christians mean by resurrection, and how does it differ from reincarnation?
options: Resurrection and reincarnation are basically the same idea of life after death.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.

Resurrection is the once-for-all bodily raising to eternal life at the end of time (modelled on Christ's resurrection); reincarnation is the soul's repeated rebirth into new bodies. They are distinct doctrines from different religious traditions.

mcqs.q: What do orthodox Christians believe about the nature of Jesus?
options: Jesus was half God and half human.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
He is fully God and fully human at the same time (the incarnation) — both natures united in one person, as defined at the Council of Chalcedon.
